<a id="agreement"></a>

## Master agreement: agreement (AGR)

ISDA, GMRA or GMSLA master agreement with its key elections. One row per master agreement per business date, keyed by AGREEMENT_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `legal-store` (lake table `legal.agreement`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (24 records); the records never changed over the period, so every later day's file is empty. Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 24 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/agreement/` + `agreement.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `AGREEMENT_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 24 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "AGREEMENT_ID": "AGR-ALDERSHOT-ISDA",
  "TYPE": "ISDA 2002 Master",
  "COUNTERPARTY_NAME": "Aldershot Pension Trust",
  "GOVERNING_LAW": "English",
  "SIGNED": "2015-12-10",
  "CLOSE_OUT_NETTING": "Enforceable",
  "ELECTIONS": {
    "AUTOMATIC_EARLY_TERMINATION": false,
    "CROSS_DEFAULT": "3% of shareholders' equity",
    "SET_OFF": true,
    "TERMINATION_CURRENCY": "USD",
    "ADDITIONAL_TERMINATION_EVENTS": "Rating downgrade below BBB-",
    "PROTOCOLS": "ISDA 2020 IBOR Fallbacks; 2018 US Resolution Stay"
  },
  "COUNTERPARTY": "CP-ALDERSHOT",
  "CSAS": [
    "CSA-ALDERSHOT-FRA",
    "CSA-ALDERSHOT-LDN",
    "CSA-ALDERSHOT-NY",
    "CSA-ALDERSHOT-TKY"
  ]
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AGREEMENT_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^AGR-` | `"AGR-ALDERSHOT-ISDA"` |
| `TYPE` | string | required | The master agreement form, for example the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement. | — | `"ISDA 2002 Master"` |
| `COUNTERPARTY_NAME` | string | required | The legal entity that signed the agreement with the bank. | — | `"Aldershot Pension Trust"` |
| `GOVERNING_LAW` | string | required | The law the agreement is read under, which decides how close-out netting is enforced. | one of `English`, `New York` | `"English"` |
| `SIGNED` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date the agreement was signed. | — | `"2015-12-10"` |
| `CLOSE_OUT_NETTING` | string | required | Whether a legal opinion confirms that on default the trades net to one amount; only then may exposure be netted. | — | `"Enforceable"` |
| `ELECTIONS` | object | required | The master agreement's elections, one object: AUTOMATIC_EARLY_TERMINATION (boolean), CROSS_DEFAULT (the threshold as text), SET_OFF (boolean), TERMINATION_CURRENCY (ISO 4217), ADDITIONAL_TERMINATION_EVENTS and PROTOCOLS (text). | links to `election` | {…} |
| `ELECTIONS.AUTOMATIC_EARLY_TERMINATION` | boolean | required | Whether the trades end by themselves on certain defaults, without a notice. | — | `false` |
| `ELECTIONS.CROSS_DEFAULT` | string | required | The threshold above which a default on other debt is a default under this agreement. | — | `"3% of shareholders' equity"` |
| `ELECTIONS.SET_OFF` | boolean | required | Whether amounts owed under other contracts may be set off against the close-out amount. | — | `true` |
| `ELECTIONS.TERMINATION_CURRENCY` | string | required | The currency the close-out amount is paid in. | — | `"USD"` |
| `ELECTIONS.ADDITIONAL_TERMINATION_EVENTS` | string | required | Further events, such as a downgrade, that let a party end the trades. | — | `"Rating downgrade below BBB-"` |
| `ELECTIONS.PROTOCOLS` | string | required | The ISDA protocols both parties adhered to, which amend the agreement. | — | `"ISDA 2020 IBOR Fallbacks; 2018 US Resolution Stay"` |
| `COUNTERPARTY` | string | required | The counterparty that signed the agreement: a COUNTERPARTY_ID of the core pack's counterparty kind (CP-…). | pattern `^CP-`; links to `counterparty` | `"CP-ALDERSHOT"` |
| `CSAS` | array of strings | required | The credit support annexes under this agreement, one per bank legal entity it covers (decision 9): CSA_IDs of the csa kind (CSA-<counterparty>-<legal entity>); empty when the agreement has none. | links to `csa` | [4 values] |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 24 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `AGREEMENT_ID` per `business_date`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `AGREEMENT_ID`, `TYPE`, `COUNTERPARTY_NAME`, `GOVERNING_LAW`, `SIGNED`, `CLOSE_OUT_NETTING`, `ELECTIONS`, `COUNTERPARTY`, `CSAS` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Each day: the records new or changed that day (or all of them); Drishti keeps the rest from the day before.
- Unique: `AGREEMENT_ID` per business_date.
- `AGREEMENT_ID` matches `^AGR-`.

<a id="collateral-balance"></a>

## Collateral balance: collateral-balance (COLL)

Collateral held and posted under a CSA, by asset, after haircuts. One row per collateral balance per business date, keyed by BALANCE_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `collateral-store` (lake table `collateral.collateral-balance`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (76 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (76–76 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 4,560 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/collateral-balance/` + `collateral-balance.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `BALANCE_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BALANCE_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^COLL-` | `"COLL-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `HELD` | integer | required | The collateral the bank has received from the counterparty, after haircut: the sum of its Held positions' VALUE (market value less the CSA haircut; F3). | unit: USD | `0` |
| `POSTED` | integer | required | The collateral the bank has delivered to the counterparty, after haircut: the sum of its Posted positions' VALUE (F3). | unit: USD | `15251373` |
| `NET` | integer | required | HELD minus POSTED after haircuts: positive when the bank holds more collateral than it has posted, negative when it has posted more. | unit: USD | `-15251373` |
| `AS_OF` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date the balance is valued on: the business date of the file. | — | `"2026-07-08"` |
| `POSITIONS` | array of objects | required | The collateral assets behind the balance, one element per asset held or posted, with its market value, haircut and value after the haircut. | — | [3 objects] |
| `POSITIONS[].ASSET` | string | required | The cash or security that is held or posted. | — | `"Solaris Energy Corp. 2031"` |
| `POSITIONS[].DIRECTION` | string | required | Whether the bank posted the asset or received it. | one of `Posted`, `Received`, `Held` | `"Posted"` |
| `POSITIONS[].MARKET_VALUE` | integer | required | The current market value of the asset before the haircut. | unit: USD | `5109338` |
| `POSITIONS[].HAIRCUT` | number | required | The share taken off the market value to allow for the price moving before the asset can be sold. The CSA sets it by asset type and maturity. | unit: fraction of the market value (0.005 is 0.5%) | `0.005` |
| `POSITIONS[].VALUE` | integer | required | The market value after the haircut, the amount that counts as collateral. | unit: USD | `5083791` |
| `CSA` | string | required | The CSA the collateral is exchanged under: a CSA_ID of the csa kind (CSA-…). | pattern `^CSA-`; links to `csa` | `"CSA-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `NETTING_SET` | string | required | The netting set the collateral secures: a NETTING_SET_ID of the netting-set kind (NS-<counterparty>-<legal entity>). | pattern `^NS-`; links to `netting-set` | `"NS-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |

## Credit limit: credit-limit (LIM)

PFE limit by tenor bucket for a counterparty, with utilisation. One row per credit limit per business date, keyed by LIMIT_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `credit-store` (lake table `credit.credit-limit`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (24 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (24–24 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 1,440 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/credit-limit/` + `credit-limit.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `LIMIT_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LIMIT_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^LIM-` | `"LIM-ALDERSHOT"` |
| `COUNTERPARTY_NAME` | string | required | The legal entity the limit applies to. | — | `"Aldershot Pension Trust"` |
| `MEASURE` | string | required | The exposure measure the limit is set on, for example the peak of the 95th-percentile potential future exposure. | — | `"PFE 95 peak"` |
| `LIMIT` | number | required | The most exposure the bank accepts to the counterparty on this measure. | unit: USD | `7980000000.0` |
| `USED` | integer | required | The exposure measured today against the limit. | unit: USD | `6001569387` |
| `UTILISATION` | number | required | The share of the limit that is used: USED divided by LIMIT, as a fraction. Above 1 is a breach. | unit: fraction of the limit (0.6671 is 66.71%) | `0.666921` |
| `STATUS` | string | required | The limit's state from UTILISATION: Within limit below 80% used, Early warning from 80% to 100%, Breach above 100%. | one of `Early warning`, `Within limit` | `"Within limit"` |
| `BUCKETS` | array of objects | required | The limit and its use by maturity bucket, one element per bucket (0-1Y, 1-3Y, 3-5Y, 5-10Y, 10Y+): LIMIT, USED and UTILISATION. | — | [5 objects] |
| `BUCKETS[].BUCKET` | string | required | The range of years to maturity the limit is split into; exposure on trades that mature within it is counted against it. | one of `0-1Y`, `1-3Y`, `10Y+`, `3-5Y`, `5-10Y` | `"0-1Y"` |
| `BUCKETS[].LIMIT` | integer | required | The limit that applies to this tenor bucket. | unit: USD | `7980000000` |
| `BUCKETS[].USED` | integer | required | The exposure in this tenor bucket. | unit: USD | `4733741826` |
| `BUCKETS[].UTILISATION` | number | required | The share of the bucket's limit that is used: USED divided by LIMIT, as a fraction. Above 1 is a breach. | unit: fraction of the limit (0.567 is 56.7%) | `0.567351` |
| `COUNTERPARTY` | string | required | The counterparty the limit is set for: a COUNTERPARTY_ID of the core pack's counterparty kind (CP-…). | pattern `^CP-`; links to `counterparty` | `"CP-ALDERSHOT"` |
| `APPROVED_BY` | string | required | The committee or officer that approved the limit. | — | `"Credit Risk Committee"` |
| `REVIEW_DUE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date the limit is next due for credit review (YYYY-MM-DD). | — | `"2027-03-19"` |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CSA_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^CSA-` | `"CSA-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `MARGIN_TYPE` | string | required | Variation margin (VM) covers today's value; initial margin (IM) covers how it may move before a default is closed out. | one of `VM`, `VM + IM` | `"VM"` |
| `CSA_CURRENCY` | string | required | The currency the CSA's amounts are in (thresholds, minimum transfer amounts, independent amount) and calls are made in. | — | `"USD"` |
| `THRESHOLD_US` | number | required | The exposure the counterparty may have to the bank before the bank must post collateral. | unit: USD | `10000000.0` |
| `THRESHOLD_THEM` | number | required | The exposure the bank accepts before the counterparty must post collateral. | unit: USD | `10000000.0` |
| `MTA` | integer | required | The smallest collateral movement either side may call. | unit: USD | `500000` |

| `MPOR_DAYS` | integer | required | The margin period of risk, in business days, assumed between the last margin received and closing out a defaulted counterparty. | unit: business days | `10` |

| `ELIGIBLE[].ASSET` | string | required | An asset the counterparty may deliver as collateral. | one of `G7 government bonds 1-5Y`, `G7 government bonds 5-10Y`, `G7 government bonds < 1Y`, `USD, EUR, GBP cash` | `"USD, EUR, GBP cash"` |
| `ELIGIBLE[].HAIRCUT` | number | required | The share taken off the asset's value when it is counted as collateral. | — | `0.0` |
| `AGREEMENT` | string | required | The master agreement the CSA belongs to: an AGREEMENT_ID of the agreement kind (AGR-…). | pattern `^AGR-`; links to `agreement` | `"AGR-ALDERSHOT-ISDA"` |
| `COUNTERPARTY` | string | required | The counterparty of the CSA: a COUNTERPARTY_ID of the core pack's counterparty kind (CP-…). | pattern `^CP-`; links to `counterparty` | `"CP-ALDERSHOT"` |
| `LEGAL_ENTITY` | string | required | The bank legal entity the CSA is signed by (one CSA per agreement and legal entity, decision 9). | links to `legal-entity` | `"LE-FRA"` |
| `NETTING_SETS` | array of strings | required | The netting sets margined under the CSA: NETTING_SET_IDs of the netting-set kind (NS-<counterparty>-<legal entity>). | links to `netting-set` | [1 values] |
| `COLLATERAL_BALANCES` | array of strings | required | The collateral balances held or posted under the CSA, one per netting set: BALANCE_IDs of the collateral-balance kind (COLL-…). | links to `collateral-balance` | [1 values] |

<a id="cva"></a>

## CVA / XVA: cva (CVA)

Credit, debit and funding valuation adjustments with sensitivities. One row per cva / xva per business date, keyed by RESULT_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `credit-store` (lake table `credit.cva`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (76 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (69–75 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 4,373 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/cva/` + `cva.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `RESULT_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 4,373 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json

  "RESULT_ID": "CVA-CASCADIA-FRA",
  "CVA": -44037,
  "DVA": 1363,
  "FVA": -14293,
  "KVA": -41215,
  "CS01": -795,
  "COMPONENTS": [
    {
      "NAME": "CVA",
      "AMOUNT": -44139
    },
    {
      "NAME": "DVA",
      "AMOUNT": 1363
    },
    "… 2 more elements of the same shape"
  ],
  "SENSITIVITIES": [
    {
      "FACTOR": "Counterparty spread",
      "BUMP": "+1 bp",
      "DELTA": -795
    },
    {
      "FACTOR": "USD rates",
      "BUMP": "+1 bp",
      "DELTA": 177
    },

  ],

}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RESULT_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^CVA-` | `"CVA-CASCADIA-FRA"` |
| `CVA` | integer | required | The expected loss from the counterparty defaulting, valued at market spreads and taken off the value of the trades. | unit: USD | `-44037` |
| `DVA` | integer | required | The mirror image of CVA: the gain from the bank's own possible default, which reduces what it would owe. | unit: USD | `1363` |
| `FVA` | integer | required | The cost, or benefit, of funding the collateral and the hedges of uncollateralised trades. | unit: USD | `-14293` |
| `KVA` | integer | required | The cost of holding regulatory capital against the trades over their life. | unit: USD | `-41215` |
| `CS01` | integer | required | The change in the CVA for a one basis point rise in the counterparty's credit spread. | unit: USD per bp | `-795` |
| `COMPONENTS` | array of objects | required | The valuation adjustments that make up the total, one element per adjustment (CVA, DVA, FVA, KVA): NAME and AMOUNT in USD, a cost negative. | — | [4 objects] |
| `COMPONENTS[].NAME` | string | required | The valuation adjustment: CVA, DVA, FVA or KVA. | one of `CVA`, `DVA`, `FVA`, `KVA` | `"CVA"` |
| `COMPONENTS[].AMOUNT` | integer | required | The adjustment's amount, from the bank's side: a cost is negative. | unit: USD | `-44139` |
| `SENSITIVITIES` | array of objects | required | The adjustment's sensitivities, one element per risk factor (counterparty spread, USD and EUR rates, FX vol, recovery): FACTOR, BUMP (+1 bp, +1 vol, +1%) and DELTA in USD. | — | [5 objects] |
| `SENSITIVITIES[].FACTOR` | string | required | The market input that is bumped to see how the adjustment changes. | one of `Counterparty spread`, `EUR rates`, `FX vol`, `Recovery`, `USD rates` | `"Counterparty spread"` |
| `SENSITIVITIES[].BUMP` | string | required | The size of the move applied to the factor. | one of `+1 bp`, `+1 vol`, `+1%` | `"+1 bp"` |
| `SENSITIVITIES[].DELTA` | integer | required | The change in the adjustment for the bump. | unit: USD | `-795` |
| `NETTING_SET` | string | required | The netting set the adjustment is computed for: a NETTING_SET_ID of the netting-set kind (NS-<counterparty>-<legal entity>). | pattern `^NS-`; links to `netting-set` | `"NS-CASCADIA-FRA"` |
| `CREDIT_CURVE` | string | optional (filled in 38% of rows) | The counterparty's credit curve the default probabilities come from: a CURVE_ID of the market-data pack's credit-curve kind (CDS-…). | pattern `^CDS-`; links to `credit-curve` | `"CDS-CASCADIA"` |

- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.

## Margin call: margin-call (MC)

A variation or initial margin call and its settlement status. One row per margin call per business date, keyed by CALL_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `collateral-store` (lake table `collateral.margin-call`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (152 records); the records never changed over the period, so every later day's file is empty. Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 152 rows in all.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/margin-call/` + `margin-call.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `CALL_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |

| `DIRECTION` | string | required | Who calls on whom. | one of `We call`, `They call` | `"They call"` |

| `DISPUTE_AMOUNT` | number | required | The part of the call the other party does not accept. Undisputed margin is still due on time; the difference goes to dispute resolution. | unit: call currency | `0` |

| `NETTING_SET` | string | required | The netting set the call is for: a NETTING_SET_ID of the netting-set kind (NS-<counterparty>-<legal entity>). | pattern `^NS-`; links to `netting-set` | `"NS-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `CSA` | string | required | The CSA the call is made under: a CSA_ID of the csa kind (CSA-…). | pattern `^CSA-`; links to `csa` | `"CSA-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `CURRENCY` | string | required | The currency of the call's amounts, ISO 4217. | — | `"USD"` |

Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 4,560 rows in all.

| Key field | `NETTING_SET_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |

| `NET_MTM` | number | required | The sum of the members' mark to market, positive and negative together. Netting lets a loss on one trade cancel a gain on another if the counterparty defaults. | unit: USD | `-135735441.598289` |
| `COLLATERAL` | integer | required | The net collateral against the netting set after haircut: what is held less what has been posted, each holding at its collateral value (market value less the CSA haircut; F3). Equal to the collateral balance's NET. | unit: USD | `-111102172` |
| `LIMIT` | number | required | The limit on the counterparty's peak potential future exposure approved for this netting set. | unit: USD | `3568000000.0` |
| `CVA` | integer | required | The reduction in the value of the trades for the risk that the counterparty defaults before they mature. | unit: USD | `-1565490` |
| `TRADES` | array of objects | required (filled in 94% of rows) | The netting set's member trades, one element per trade with its status, product, asset class, currency, book, notional and MtM; empty when the set has no live trade on the date. | — | [141 objects] |

| `TRADES[].PRODUCT` | string | required | The kind of instrument the trade is. | — | `"Year-on-year inflation swap"` |
| `TRADES[].ASSET_CLASS` | string | required | The member trade's asset class. | — | `"Inflation"` |
| `TRADES[].CURRENCY` | string | required | The member trade's currency, ISO 4217. | one of `AUD`, `CAD`, `CHF`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`, `USD` | `"JPY"` |
| `TRADES[].BOOK` | string | required | The book the member trade sits in: a BOOK_ID of the core pack's book kind (BOOK-…). | pattern `^BOOK-`; links to `book` | `"BOOK-INFL-3"` |
| `TRADES[].NOTIONAL` | number | required | The reference amount of the trade, in the trade's own currency. | unit: trade currency | `1038030000.0` |
| `TRADES[].MATURITY` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date the trade ends. | — | `"2028-04-14"` |

<a id="sa-ccr"></a>

## SA-CCR exposure: sa-ccr (SACCR)

Regulatory EAD: replacement cost, PFE add-ons by asset class, multiplier. One row per sa-ccr exposure per business date, keyed by CALC_ID. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `credit-store` (lake table `credit.sa-ccr`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (76 records); the records never changed over the period, so every later day's file is empty. Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 76 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/sa-ccr/` + `sa-ccr.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `CALC_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CALC_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^SACCR-` | `"SACCR-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `REPLACEMENT_COST` | integer | required | The loss if the counterparty defaulted today and the trades were replaced at current market value, less collateral; never below zero. | unit: USD | `0` |
| `ADD_ON` | integer | required | The potential increase in exposure over the next year, built from the add-ons of each asset class with supervisory factors and correlations. | unit: USD | `9479416` |
| `MULTIPLIER` | number | required | A factor between 5% and 1 that reduces the add-on when the netting set is over-collateralised or its value is negative. | unit: factor | `0.6819` |
| `EAD` | integer | required | The SA-CCR exposure: 1.4 times the replacement cost plus the potential future exposure, where the potential future exposure is the multiplier times the add-on. | unit: USD | `9049620` |
| `RWA` | integer | required | The exposure at default multiplied by the risk weight of the counterparty. Capital is a percentage of it. | unit: USD | `1809924` |
| `ADD_ONS` | array of objects | required | The potential-future-exposure add-ons, one element per asset class present (Interest rate, Foreign exchange, Credit, Equity, Commodity): ASSET_CLASS and ADD_ON in USD. | — | [1 objects] |
| `ADD_ONS[].ASSET_CLASS` | string | required | The SA-CCR asset class: Interest rate, Foreign exchange, Credit, Equity or Commodity. | one of `Commodity`, `Credit`, `Equity`, `Foreign exchange`, `Interest rate` | `"Interest rate"` |
| `ADD_ONS[].ADD_ON` | integer | required | The asset class's aggregate add-on (sum of its hedging sets' effective notionals times their supervisory factors). | unit: USD | `9479416` |
| `HEDGING_SETS` | array of objects | required | The hedging sets of the calculation, one element per asset class and hedging set (a currency for rates and FX): EFFECTIVE_NOTIONAL in USD and the supervisory factor SF (a fraction). | — | [5 objects] |
| `HEDGING_SETS[].ASSET_CLASS` | string | required | The regulatory asset class: interest rate, FX, credit, equity or commodity. | one of `Commodity`, `Credit`, `Equity`, `Foreign exchange`, `Interest rate` | `"Interest rate"` |
| `HEDGING_SETS[].HEDGING_SET` | string | required | The group of trades within an asset class that can offset one another, for example by currency for interest rates. | one of `AUD`, `CAD`, `CHF`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`, `USD` | `"JPY"` |
| `HEDGING_SETS[].EFFECTIVE_NOTIONAL` | integer | required | The hedging set's notional after supervisory delta and maturity adjustments and netting inside the set. | unit: USD | `-216135527` |
| `HEDGING_SETS[].SF` | number | required | The supervisory factor, as a fraction, applied to the effective notional to get the add-on. | unit: fraction of the effective notional (0.005 is 0.5%) | `0.005` |
| `NETTING_SET` | string | required | The netting set the calculation is for: a NETTING_SET_ID of the netting-set kind (NS-<counterparty>-<legal entity>). | pattern `^NS-`; links to `netting-set` | `"NS-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `ALPHA` | number | required | The SA-CCR alpha multiplier applied to replacement cost plus PFE (regulatory 1.4). | unit: factor | `1.4` |

<a id="simulation-run"></a>

## Exposure simulation run: simulation-run (XRUN)

An upstream exposure simulation of a business date: its paths, its grid of future dates (primary and look-back), its model and seed; the exposure engine reads it beside the paths (EXPOSURE_GUIDE.md section 15.2). One row per simulation run and business date, keyed by RUN_ID; the newest complete run of a date answers. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `exposure-store` (lake table `risk.simulation-run`). Delivered **per close of business**: one file per business date (`BUSINESS_DATE` 2026-09-30 in the test data), split into numbered parts when large; each date's file is the **full set** of that date (1 records), never a change on the day before.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/simulation-run/` + `simulation-run.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `RUN_ID` |
| Date field | `BUSINESS_DATE` (in every record: the business date it belongs to; the lake's partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | `RUN_ID`, `CALIBRATION`, `PATHS`, `STATUS`, `BATCH_ID` |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | the full set of its date |

### One sample record

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RUN_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^XR-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]+$`; links to `simulation-run` | `"XR-2026-09-30-01"` |
| `BUSINESS_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The close the run starts from (t0). | — | `"2026-09-30"` |
| `MARKET_DATA_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The market data the run calibrated to (normally the business date). | — | `"2026-09-30"` |
| `MODEL` | string | required | The scenario model, as free text. | — | `"One correlated Brownian factor per asset class (rates, FX,…` |
| `MODEL_VERSION` | string | required | The simulator's version; with SEED, market data and trade versions the run is reproducible upstream. | — | `"drishti-testgen-ccr-1.0"` |
| `CALIBRATION` | string | required | REAL_WORLD (for PFE and limits) or RISK_NEUTRAL (for CVA and pricing) or STRESSED. | — | `"REAL_WORLD"` |
| `PATHS` | integer | required | The number of simulated market scenarios; every trade's values are on the same paths. | — | `200` |
| `SEED` | string | required | The random generator's seed of the run. | — | `"ccr\|XR-2026-09-30-01"` |
| `ANTITHETIC` | boolean | required | true when paths 2k and 2k+1 are antithetic pairs. | — | `false` |
| `GRID_DATES` | array of dates | required | The future dates the trades were valued at: the primary dates where exposure is reported and the look-back dates a margin period of risk before them. | — | [24 values] |
| `GRID_ROLE` | array of strings | required | One per grid date, in GRID_DATES order: PRIMARY (exposure is reported) or LOOKBACK (used only for collateral, the margin period of risk). | — | [24 values] |
| `LOOKBACK_OF` | array of numbers | required | One per grid date: for a LOOKBACK point the index of the PRIMARY point it serves; -1 for a primary point. *24 values in the test data* | — | [24 numbers] |
| `GRID_TENORS` | array of strings | required | One per grid date: a primary date's tenor label (1W.. 10Y), null for a look-back date; absent, the engine labels by the nearest standard tenor. | — | [24 values] |
| `LOOKBACK_DAYS` | integer | required | How many business days before each primary date its look-back date is: the margin period of risk the run assumes. | unit: business days | `10` |
| `VALUE_BASIS` | string | required | FUTURE (each MTM in USD of its grid date; Drishti discounts for CVA) or DISCOUNTED (in today's USD by the run's numeraire). | — | `"FUTURE"` |
| `CURRENCY` | string | required | The currency of every MTM vector: must be USD. | — | `"USD"` |
| `PRECISION` | string | required | float32 or float64: how the path values are stored. | — | `"float64"` |
| `CREDIT_PATHS` | boolean | required | true when the run also wrote credit-path rows (wrong-way risk). | — | `false` |
| `NETTING_SETS` | integer | required | How many netting sets the run simulated (a count, not an id), as an integer. | links to `netting-set` | `8` |
| `TRADES` | integer | required | The number of trades the run wrote paths for. | — | `523` |
| `ROWS` | integer | required | The number of exposure-path rows the run wrote; the run is complete when the lake holds that many. | — | `7540` |
| `BATCH_ID` | string | required | The run's batch id; every exposure-path row of the run carries the same. | — | `"XB-2026-09-30-01"` |
| `COMPUTED_AT` | timestamp (ISO-8601) | required | When the run finished, ISO-8601 UTC. | — | `"2026-09-30T23:40:00Z"` |
| `STATUS` | string | required | The run's status: complete is read; a run of any other status is not. | — | `"complete"` |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 1 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `RUN_ID` per `BUSINESS_DATE`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `RUN_ID`, `BUSINESS_DATE`, `MARKET_DATA_DATE`, `MODEL`, `MODEL_VERSION`, `CALIBRATION`, `PATHS`, `SEED`, `ANTITHETIC`, `GRID_DATES`, `GRID_ROLE`, `LOOKBACK_OF`, `GRID_TENORS`, `LOOKBACK_DAYS`, `VALUE_BASIS`, `CURRENCY`, `PRECISION`, `CREDIT_PATHS`, `NETTING_SETS`, `TRADES`, `ROWS`, `BATCH_ID`, `COMPUTED_AT`, `STATUS` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- One row per run and date; `GRID_DATES` increasing and after the business date; `PATHS` is the length of every path vector of the run (`DRS-5441`).
- Each date: the full set of the date in one or more files, every record with its `BUSINESS_DATE`; a later full file of the same date restates it.
- Unique: `RUN_ID` per `BUSINESS_DATE`.
- `RUN_ID` matches `^XR-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]+$`.
- `LOOKBACK_OF` has the same length on every row of one business date.

<a id="exposure-path"></a>

## Exposure path (a trade's MtM on every path at a grid date): exposure-path (XPATH)

One trade's mark to market on every path of a simulation run at one grid date, in USD (the vector column MTM); the grain every exposure is netted, collateralised and counted from (EXPOSURE_GUIDE.md section 15.3). One row per trade, grid date and run per business date, keyed by PATH_ROW_ID (<run>~<trade>~<grid index>); sparse by maturity. Read by the **counterparty-risk** pack's connector `exposure-store` (lake table `risk.exposure-path`). Delivered **per close of business**: one file per business date (`BUSINESS_DATE` 2026-09-30 in the test data), split into numbered parts when large; each date's file is the **full set** of that date (7,540 records), never a change on the day before.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/counterparty-risk/exposure-path/` + `exposure-path.tar!/exposure-path/YYYY-MM-DD/cob.part-NNN.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `PATH_ROW_ID` |
| Date field | `BUSINESS_DATE` (in every record: the business date it belongs to; the lake's partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | `TRADE_ID`, `NETTING_SET`, `COUNTERPARTY`, `LEGAL_ENTITY`, `DIVISION`, `DESK`, `TT_BOOK`, `LIMIT_LETTER`, `ASSET_CLASS`, `PRODUCT`, `SOURCE_SYSTEM`, `MATURITY_DATE`, `NOTIONAL`, `GRID_INDEX`, `GRID_DATE`, `RUN_ID`, `BATCH_ID`, `STATUS` |
| Vector fields | `MTM` |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | the full set of its date |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 7,540 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "PATH_ROW_ID": "XR-2026-09-30-01~CLY-3000280~0",
  "BUSINESS_DATE": "2026-09-30",
  "RUN_ID": "XR-2026-09-30-01",
  "TRADE_ID": "CLY-3000280",
  "SOURCE_SYSTEM": "CALYPSO",
  "NETTING_SET": "NS-ALDERSHOT-FRA",
  "COUNTERPARTY": "CP-ALDERSHOT",
  "LEGAL_ENTITY": "LE-FRA",
  "DIVISION": "DIV-TREASURY",
  "DESK": "DESK-SFT",
  "TT_BOOK": "BOOK-SFT-1",
  "LIMIT_LETTER": "LL-0001",
  "ASSET_CLASS": "Securities financing",
  "PRODUCT": "Tri-party repo",
  "NOTIONAL": 260700000.0,
  "MATURITY_DATE": "2027-02-15",
  "GRID_INDEX": 0,
  "GRID_DATE": "2026-10-07",
  "MTM": [
    -523841,
    -1015981,
    -712385,
    "… 197 more numbers (one per simulation path, path 0 first)"
  ],
  "STATUS": "ok",
  "PRICER": "testgen-factor-walk",
  "BATCH_ID": "XB-2026-09-30-01"
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PATH_ROW_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^XR-[^~]+~.+~[0-9]+$` | `"XR-2026-09-30-01~CLY-3000280~0"` |
| `BUSINESS_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The close of business the run starts from (t0); the lake's partition. | — | `"2026-09-30"` |
| `RUN_ID` | string | required | The simulation run the row belongs to: a RUN_ID of the simulation-run kind (XR-<date>-<nn>), the same on every row of the run. | pattern `^XR-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]+$`; links to `simulation-run` | `"XR-2026-09-30-01"` |
| `TRADE_ID` | string | required | The trade valued on the paths: a TRADE_ID of the trading pack's trade kind (ENDUR digits, CLY-…, MX-…), as text. | pattern `^((MX\|CLY)-)?\d+$`; links to `trade` | `"CLY-3000280"` |
| `SOURCE_SYSTEM` | string | required | The trade's booking system: ENDUR, CALYPSO or MUREX. | one of `CALYPSO`, `ENDUR`, `MUREX` | `"CALYPSO"` |
| `NETTING_SET` | string | required | The netting set the trade belongs to (its membership wins when they differ). | pattern `^NS-`; links to `netting-set` | `"NS-ALDERSHOT-FRA"` |
| `COUNTERPARTY` | string | required | The trade's counterparty, denormalised from its netting set: a COUNTERPARTY_ID of the core pack's counterparty kind (CP-…). | pattern `^CP-`; links to `counterparty` | `"CP-ALDERSHOT"` |
| `LEGAL_ENTITY` | string | required | The bank's legal entity that booked the trade: an ENTITY_ID of the core pack's legal-entity kind (LE-…). | pattern `^LE-`; links to `legal-entity` | `"LE-FRA"` |
| `DIVISION` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The division of the trade's desk (DIV-…): the top level column of the hierarchy MGMT (DIVISION > DESK > TT_BOOK, VAR_GUIDE.md section 15.14), as the trade's VaR records carry it. A row that leaves it empty sits under the (Blank) division. | seen: `DIV-MARKETS`, `DIV-TREASURY` | `"DIV-TREASURY"` |
| `DESK` | string | required | The desk the trade is booked on: a DESK_ID of the core pack's desk kind (DESK-…). | pattern `^DESK-`; links to `desk` | `"DESK-SFT"` |
| `TT_BOOK` | string | required | The book the trade is booked in: a BOOK_ID of the core pack's book kind (BOOK-…). | pattern `^BOOK-`; links to `book` | `"BOOK-SFT-1"` |
| `LIMIT_LETTER` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The trade's limit letter, as its VaR records carry it: the level column of the hierarchy LL (LIMIT_LETTER > DESK, VAR_GUIDE.md section 15.14). Every hierarchy is built from promoted columns: a row that leaves a level column empty sits under a (Blank) node at that level, and a table that does not promote the column puts every row there, with a DRS-5211 warning. | — | `"LL-0001"` |
| `ASSET_CLASS` | string | required | The trade's asset class, denormalised from the netting set's member row (used by the asset scope). | one of `Commodity`, `Credit`, `Equity`, `FX`, `Fixed income`, `Inflation`, `Money market`, `Rates`, `Securities financing`, `Structured` | `"Securities financing"` |
| `PRODUCT` | string | required | The trade's product name, denormalised from the netting set's member row (e.g. Basis swap (float/float)). | — | `"Tri-party repo"` |
| `NOTIONAL` | number | required | The trade's notional as its netting set lists it, in the trade's currency; denormalised for people and checks. | unit: trade currency | `260700000.0` |
| `MATURITY_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The trade's maturity: after it plus 10 business days a missing grid row means the trade is worth 0. | — | `"2027-02-15"` |
| `GRID_INDEX` | integer | required | The position of the date in the run's grid. | — | `0` |
| `GRID_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The future date the values are for. | — | `"2026-10-07"` |
| `MTM` | array of numbers | required | The trade's mark to market on each simulated path at the grid date, from the bank's side. *200 values in the test data* | unit: USD | [200 numbers] |
| `STATUS` | string | required | ok, proxied (an approximate model) or failed (no values). | — | `"ok"` |
| `PRICER` | string | required | The pricer the simulator valued the trade with (testgen-factor-walk in the test data). | — | `"testgen-factor-walk"` |
| `BATCH_ID` | string | required | The run's batch: equal to the simulation-run's BATCH_ID. | — | `"XB-2026-09-30-01"` |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 7,540 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `PATH_ROW_ID` per `BUSINESS_DATE`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `PATH_ROW_ID`, `BUSINESS_DATE`, `RUN_ID`, `TRADE_ID`, `SOURCE_SYSTEM`, `NETTING_SET`, `COUNTERPARTY`, `LEGAL_ENTITY`, `DESK`, `TT_BOOK`, `ASSET_CLASS`, `PRODUCT`, `NOTIONAL`, `MATURITY_DATE`, `GRID_INDEX`, `GRID_DATE`, `MTM`, `STATUS`, `PRICER`, `BATCH_ID` (the contract's required fields); every row of the test data also fills `DIVISION`, `LIMIT_LETTER`.
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- One row per (`RUN_ID`, `TRADE_ID`, `GRID_INDEX`) (a duplicate fails the load); `MTM` has exactly the run's `PATHS` numbers, no `null`, `NaN` or infinity (`DRS-5444`); `GRID_DATE` = the run's `GRID_DATES[GRID_INDEX]`; rows to the trade's maturity; one `BATCH_ID` per run (`DRS-5441`).
- Each date: the full set of the date in one or more files, every record with its `BUSINESS_DATE`; a later full file of the same date restates it.
- Unique: `PATH_ROW_ID` per `BUSINESS_DATE`.
- `PATH_ROW_ID` matches `^XR-[^~]+~.+~[0-9]+$`.
- `MTM` has the same length on every row of one business date.
